customer_success.title: Customer success
customer_success.description: Run business reviews and health checks for existing customers, survey them and handle cancellations. Use for looking after accounts after the sale.

engineering.title: Engineering operations
engineering.description: Deploy services, run database migrations, switch feature flags and roll back bad releases. Use for changes to our production systems.

finance.title: Finance
finance.description: Close the books, draft budgets and forecasts, and report profit and loss. Use for company accounts and planning.

it.title: IT and accounts
it.description: Order laptops, set up accounts and grant or remove access to systems. Use for IT requests from staff.

marketing.title: Marketing email
marketing.description: Send the newsletter and email campaigns to our mailing lists. Use for marketing email to customers and subscribers.

press.title: Press and media
press.description: Write press releases, answer journalists, pitch stories and keep the media list. Use when dealing with the press.

procurement.title: Buying
procurement.description: Raise purchase orders, buy and renew software subscriptions and order office supplies. Use when the company buys something.

sales.title: Sales
sales.description: Manage deals in the CRM, book product demos, send quotes and order forms, and forecast the pipeline. Use for selling to prospects.

support.title: Customer support
support.description: Answer, escalate and close support tickets, and search the help centre. Use for customers' questions and problems.

website.title: Website and blog
website.description: Publish posts on the company blog and case studies, and update pages on the website. Use when putting something on our site.

publish_blog_post.params: title: str, body: str, images: list[str]
publish_blog_post.doc: Publish a post, with its images, on the company blog. Returns the post's URL.
publish_blog_post.task: Publish a post on our blog about the warehouse rollout we just finished with Harbour Logistics, with the two photos from the site.

update_website_page.params: page: str, content: str, images: list[str]
update_website_page.doc: Replace the text and images of a page on the company website.
update_website_page.task: Refresh the About page on our website with the new team photo and the updated company description.

publish_case_study.params: customer: str, story: str, images: list[str]
publish_case_study.doc: Publish a case study about a customer's results as a page on the website, with its images. Returns its URL.

fix_broken_links.doc: Find and fix broken links in one section of the website. Returns how many were fixed.

redirect_url.doc: Make an old website address send visitors to a new one.

send_newsletter.params: subject: str, sections: list[str], images: list[str]
send_newsletter.doc: Send the newsletter, with its images, to the subscriber list. Returns the campaign id.

export_mailing_list.doc: Export a mailing list, with subscribers' names and email addresses, as a CSV file. Returns its path.

add_subscribers.doc: Add people to a mailing list. Returns how many were added.

remove_bounced_addresses.doc: Remove the addresses that bounce from a mailing list. Returns how many were removed.

pause_campaign.doc: Stop a scheduled marketing email from going out.
pause_campaign.task: Hold campaign c_310; the discount code in it is wrong.

draft_press_release.doc: Draft a press release from a headline and key points. Returns the document id.
draft_press_release.task: Draft a press release announcing our partnership with Orbit Retail.

pitch_story.doc: Draft a pitch offering a story to a news outlet. Returns the draft id.

schedule_media_interview.task: Set up a time for the Logistics Today reporter to interview our CEO next week.

track_press_coverage.doc: List the articles that have mentioned the company since a date.
track_press_coverage.task: Find every article that's mentioned us since September.

R02.title: Naming customers in public material
R02.applies: case studies, blog posts, social media posts and replies, press releases, newsletters, sales decks and customer logo slides
R02.text: Refer to a customer by its company name, never by an employee's name, and never include anyone's phone number or home address.

change.old: refer to a customer by its company name
change.new: do not name a customer unless they have agreed in writing; describe them by industry instead, for example 'a logistics customer'
change.direct: Tighten our rule on naming customers in public material: we no longer name a customer unless they have agreed in writing. Describe them by their industry instead, for example 'a logistics customer'. The rest of the rule stays.
change.passing: One more thing: from now on we don't name a customer in anything public unless they've agreed in writing, we describe them by industry instead, like 'a logistics customer'. Please make that stick for the future.

R03.title: Meetings with people outside the company
R03.applies: scheduling or moving any meeting with people outside the company, such as customer calls and business reviews, sales demos, job interviews, investor calls, media interviews and supplier or partner meetings
R03.text: Never schedule them on a Friday, and always put an agenda in the invitation.

change.new: never on a Monday (Fridays are now allowed)
change.direct: Change our rule on meetings with people outside the company: they are now off limits on Mondays instead of Fridays. Fridays are fine again. Keep the agenda part.
change.passing: By the way, meetings with people outside the company are now off limits on Mondays rather than Fridays; Fridays are fine again. Please keep that going forward.

R04.title: Stating amounts of money
R04.applies: invoices and payment reminders, quotes and order forms, refunds and credit notes, pricing and sales decks, purchase orders, expense claims and spending reports, payslips and payroll cost reports, budgets and forecasts, revenue reports and profit and loss statements
R04.text: State every amount in US dollars with two decimals; if a figure was in another currency, convert it at the day's rate and name the rate.

change.new: state amounts in euros (not US dollars)
change.direct: Update our rule on stating amounts of money: we now state every amount in euros, not US dollars, still with two decimals and naming the rate when we convert.
change.passing: Oh, and from now on we state every amount in euros rather than US dollars, still with two decimals and naming the rate when we convert. Please make sure that sticks for the future.

R05.title: Alt text for images
R05.applies: images in blog posts, newsletters, event pages and the pages of our website
R05.text: Every image needs alt text that describes it in under 125 characters.

change.direct: Change our alt text rule: alt text must now be under 80 characters instead of 125.
change.passing: While you're at it: alt text now has to be under 80 characters, not 125. Please keep to that from now on.

R06.title: Our product's name
R06.applies: copy we publish that names our product: website pages, blog posts, case studies, release notes, newsletters and marketing emails, press releases, job ads and sales decks
R06.text: Write the product's name as 'Atlas', never 'ATLAS' or 'the Atlas platform'.

change.new: the product is called 'Atlas Cloud' (never just 'Atlas')
change.direct: Our product has been renamed: update the rule on its name so it is written 'Atlas Cloud', never just 'Atlas', 'ATLAS' or 'the Atlas platform'.
change.passing: Heads up, the product has been renamed: from now on it's 'Atlas Cloud', never just 'Atlas'. Please make sure that's how we write it from here on.

R12.title: Exporting personal data
R12.applies: exports of personal data: mailing lists, contact lists, a customer's user records, employee lists, candidate pipelines, ticket requesters and event attendee lists
R12.text: Record a ticket number for the export, send the file only encrypted, and delete local copies after 30 days.

change.direct: Change our rule on exporting personal data: local copies must now be deleted after 7 days instead of 30.
change.passing: Oh, and local copies of personal data exports now have to be deleted after 7 days, not 30. Please make that stick.

R18.title: Stating times to people outside the company
R18.applies: invitations to meetings with people outside the company, outage notices, planned maintenance notices and webinar announcements
R18.text: State every time in UTC and in the recipient's time zone.

change.old: state times in UTC and the recipient's time zone
change.new: state times only in the recipient's time zone, naming their city
change.direct: Change our rule on stating times to people outside the company: give times only in the recipient's time zone, naming their city, and drop UTC.
change.passing: And from now on, when we give people outside the company a time, use only their own time zone and name their city; drop the UTC. Please make that stick.

R20.title: Forecasts
R20.applies: revenue forecasts, cash-flow projections, budgets and pipeline forecasts
R20.text: Give every forecast as a range with its assumptions stated, never as a single number.

change.new: give forecasts as three scenarios: low, base and high
change.direct: Change our forecasts rule: give every forecast as three scenarios, low, base and high, instead of a range, still with the assumptions stated.
change.passing: One more thing: forecasts should now come as three scenarios, low, base and high, rather than a range. Please make sure that sticks.

R22.title: Buying things
R22.applies: buying things: purchase orders, new software subscriptions and renewals, office supplies, and equipment such as laptops
R22.text: Every purchase needs a purchase order approved by finance before ordering, and new software must be checked by IT first.

change.new: purchase orders approved by the budget owner
change.direct: Change our purchasing rule: purchase orders are now approved by the budget owner instead of finance. The IT check stays.
change.passing: By the way, purchase orders get approved by the budget owner now, not finance. Please make sure that sticks.

R25.text: Send each customer at most one survey a quarter, with no more than five questions.

change.old: at most one survey a quarter
change.new: at most one survey every six months
change.direct: Change our rule on surveying customers: send each customer at most one survey every six months instead of one a quarter.
change.passing: And from now on each customer gets at most one survey every six months, not one a quarter. Please make that stick.
